experiment.purpose: First controlled fine-tune: a LoRA adapter on an open-weight Qwen2.5 foundation model so any improvement claim is a clean comparison against the preserved baseline (webloom-ai-baseline-0.1.0) on the untouched holdout split. Targets the Phase 2 baseline failures: contract/schema drift, envelope-wrapped generative outputs, over-confidence, under-extraction and hallucination.

foundationSelection.tokenizer: Qwen/Qwen2.5 tokenizer (151936-entry vocab, shared across the Qwen2.5 family, so prompts are byte-identical to the baseline's serving prompts)
foundationSelection.inferenceBackend: OpenAI-compatible local server — bundled finetune/scripts/serve_model.py (transformers), or vLLM/llama.cpp/MLX — serving base + selected adapter merged in-process
selectedBecause: Same Qwen2.5 family, tokenizer and chat template as the registered baseline foundation model — prompt formatting is identical, one confound removed from the comparison.

1.54B bf16 weights (~3 GB) train AND serve inside 8 GB unified memory on the Apple M3 development Mac: local inference compatibility and reasonable memory requirements, no paid cloud GPU required for the first experiment.

Strong instruction following and structured-JSON generation at small size (Qwen2.5 Instruct series), LoRA/QLoRA compatible, Apache-2.0, practical inference performance for eventual per-request deployment.

considered.whyNot: Identical to the baseline serving model (cleanest possible comparison), but untrainable on the 8 GB development Mac: 14 GB of fp16 weights, no CUDA, bitsandbytes has no macOS wheel, and MLX QLoRA of a 7B model exceeds unified memory. Would force paid cloud GPU authorization before the pipeline is even proven. Remains the recommended base for a later GPU confirmation run.
Trainable locally, but too weak to model the nested envelope contracts and would measure the size limit instead of the dataset's value.

data.notes: Model fitting uses ONLY the train split (14 examples). The validation split (6 examples) is used for eval loss and checkpoint selection — never gradient updates. The holdout split (6 examples) is never formatted, never loaded, never evaluated until the final benchmark.

quantization.rationale: QLoRA is used only when it materially reduces hardware requirements (>=7B bases on CUDA). The 1.54B base fits in 16-bit (~3 GB) on the dev Mac and any cloud GPU, so plain bf16 LoRA avoids quantization noise and keeps the experiment reproducible. Re-enable together with bitsandbytes on CUDA for a >=7B confirmation run.

training.notes: micro-batch 1 x gradient accumulation 4 keeps peak activation memory inside 8 GB unified memory while preserving an effective batch of 4 (same optimizer-step schedule as batch 2 x accum 2). warmupRatio is converted to warmup_steps by the trainer because transformers v5 exposes warmup_steps only. Epoch-level step count: ceil(14 / (1 x 4)) = 4 optimizer steps/epoch, ~32 total, checkpoints every 4 steps.

checkpointSelection.notes: Checkpoints are ranked by the composite score on the validation split; the un-fine-tuned base model is scored on the same rows as a control arm so 'improvement over the foundation model' is measured, not assumed. The holdout is untouched until the final benchmark.

inference.backend: openai-compatible local server (bundled finetune/scripts/serve_model.py; vLLM/llama.cpp/MLX also work) serving base + selected adapter merged in-process
inference.holdoutBenchmark: node eval/run.js --backend webloom --model webloom-ai-v0.1.0 --dataset holdout (next phase — untouched until then)
inference.productionStatus: opt-in candidate only; baseline remains default until the holdout benchmark proves otherwise

environment.notes: On CPU/MPS (Apple Silicon) the run uses bf16 LoRA + adamw_torch (probed at runtime; fp16 fallback). Deviations from the pinned configuration are recorded in the experiment manifest rather than hidden.
